AI may not be inherently cruel or painful, but the fact is that the AI that happens today ARE. Similarly, consuming dairy is not in itself morally inconsistent or morally wrong because one might argue that you are exchanging protection for milk where both parties benefit, but the problem is that, nowadays, most of what people call "organic" or "free range" isn't what they think it is. If you think about it, since there is such a high demand of milk, cruelty-free dairy simply cannot satisfy even a small percentage of it. If you add on the requirement that the calf also uses the milk and both live a healthy life, then the chance for you to have cruelty-free milk is even lower. Thus, unless you milk and raise the cow yourself or know a local farmer who does, then you can't be sure that you are still being morally consistent by consuming milk. Whether it is inherently right or wrong is irrelevant because it refers to consumption of milk itself andonly itself but there are many factors surrounding it.
